newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Yeltsin to meet Belarus leader next week.
newsitem.headline: Yeltsin to meet Belarus leader next week.

text.p: Russian President Boris Yeltsin and Belarussian leader Alexander Lukashenko spoke by telephone on Thursday and agreed to meet next week, the Kremlin press service said.

It said the meeting would take place next Wednesday in Moscow, making Lukashenko the second foreign leader to visit Yeltsin since he announced on September 5 that he planned to have a heart operation.

The two presidents signed a framework agreement last April on forming a loose union between Russia and Belarus. But Yeltsin has expressed concern over a conflict between Lukashenko and parliament and urged him to seek a compromise.
Yeltsin moved to the Barvikha sanatorium outside Moscow last weekend after three weeks in hospital while doctors prepared him surgery. The operation is due in the next two months.
Yeltsin met his Kremlin chief-of-staff Anatoly Chubais on Thursday. A presidential spokesman said television footage of the meeting would be shown in evening news bulletins.
Interfax news agency quoted an "informed" source as saying "a film proves better than words that the president is brisk and deals with state affairs directly".

The source said rumours were being spread about Yeltsin's health which affected stock market prices. "It is clear the rumours originate from those who make money on distorted information which has nothing to do with reality," it said.
